## Comparison to other Models & Confusion Matrix {height = "40%"}

```{python}
#| title: "Accuracy Comparison"
#| width: 50%

from IPython.display import Markdown, display

acc_sorted = acc_results_df.sort_values(by="Accuracy", ascending=False)

acc_sorted.style.format({"Accuracy": "{:.4f}"}).set_table_styles([
    {"selector": "th", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
]).set_properties(
    subset=pd.IndexSlice[acc_sorted.index[0], :],  # top model row
    **{"font-weight": "bold"}
)

display(Markdown(
    "**The best-performing row (highlighted) indicates the tuned logistic\n"
    "regression model that we use in the subsequent diagnostics.**"
))

```

## ROC Curve for Each Class & KPI Metric {height = 60%}

```{python}
#| title: One-vs-Rest (OvR) ROC Curves by Political Affiliation
#| fig-cap: Each curve shows the OvR ROC for a single affiliation. AUC values in the legend indicate how easily the model distinguishes that class from all others.
#| width: 60%

y_proba_log = cross_val_predict(log_best, X, y_encoded, cv=CV, method="predict_proba")
class0_name = le.inverse_transform([0])[0]
class1_name = le.inverse_transform([1])[0]
class2_name = le.inverse_transform([2])[0]

roc_auc = roc_auc_score(y_encoded, y_proba_log, multi_class="ovr", average="macro")

y0 = (y_encoded == 0).astype(int)    
y_proba_0 = y_proba_log[:, 0]        

fpr_0, tpr_0, _ = roc_curve(y0, y_proba_0)
df_0 = pd.DataFrame({
    "model": f"{class0_name} vs Rest (Log, OOF)",
    "FPR": fpr_0,
    "TPR": tpr_0
})

y1 = (y_encoded == 1).astype(int)    
y_proba_1 = y_proba_log[:, 1]        

fpr_1, tpr_1, _ = roc_curve(y1, y_proba_1)
df_1 = pd.DataFrame({
    "model": f"{class1_name} vs Rest (Log, OOF)",
    "FPR": fpr_1,
    "TPR": tpr_1
})

y2 = (y_encoded == 2).astype(int)    
y_proba_2 = y_proba_log[:, 2]        

fpr_2, tpr_2, _ = roc_curve(y2, y_proba_2)
df_2 = pd.DataFrame({
    "model": f"{class2_name} vs Rest (Log, OOF)",
    "FPR": fpr_2,
    "TPR": tpr_2
})

roc_curve_df = pd.concat([df_0, df_1, df_2], ignore_index=True)

(
    ggplot(roc_curve_df, aes("FPR", "TPR", color="model"))
    + geom_path()
    + geom_abline(linetype="dashed")
    + labs(
        title="OvR ROC Curves – Logistic Regression (log_best, OOF)",
        x="False Positive Rate",
        y="True Positive Rate"
    )
    + theme_minimal()
    + theme(figure_size=(6.5, 3.5))  
)
```

```{python}
# Class-level ROC AUCs from the existing ROC curves
auc_0 = auc(fpr_0, tpr_0)
auc_1 = auc(fpr_1, tpr_1)
auc_2 = auc(fpr_2, tpr_2)

auc_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Affiliation": [class0_name, class1_name, class2_name],
    "ROC AUC": [auc_0, auc_1, auc_2]
}).sort_values(by="ROC AUC", ascending=False)


display(
    auc_df.style.format({"ROC AUC": "{:.3f}"})
)

display(Markdown(
    "Accuracy tells us how often the tuned logistic regression model gets the affiliation right at a single "
    "decision cutoff, while ROC AUC, both overall and by class, shows how well it separates each political "
    "group from the others across all probability thresholds. Taken together, high accuracy and strong ROC AUC "
    "scores suggest that the logistic model is not only often correct but also reliably ranks the true "
    "affiliation above the alternatives, even though a few classes remain harder to distinguish."
))
```
